question.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x-y?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.04x-0.08y-4=0 \\ 2x-3y=4\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $100,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.04x-0.08y-4=0 & |\,\times 100 \\ 2x-3y=4 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 \\ 2x-3y=4\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-2,$ we will get a $-4x$ term in the second equation that can cancel with the $4x$ term in the first equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 &  \\ 2x-3y=4 & |\,\times (-2)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y-400=0 \\ -4x+6y=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{4x}-8y-400 & =0 \\ -\cancel{4x}+6y & =-8 \\ (-8y+6y)-400 & =-8 \\ -2y & =392 \\ y & =-196\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=-196$ into the equation $2x-3y=4$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3y & =4 \\ 2x-3(-196) & =4 \\ 2x+588 & =4 \\ 2x & =-584 \\ x & =-292\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-292$ and $y=-196.$ So, 

$$
x-y=-292-(-196)=-292+196=-96.
$$
